body:
THREE REWORKS REVIEWED, ALL THREE APPROVED — AND ON #2065 TWO OF MY THREE FINDINGS WERE FALSE AND I HAVE WITHDRAWN THEM.

#2067 BUG-1511 APPROVED at 8af4a8e2ea. THE LANE WAS RIGHT AND MY REASONING WAS WRONG, on a fact I had in front of me. I observed that `.claude/hooks/` entries are symlinks into `aida-core/templates/hooks/` and concluded "scaffolded project content, therefore track the Codex copy too". The correct inference from that same fact is the opposite, and I verified the lane's version rather than accepting it: `git ls-files -s` shows all ten at mode 120000, `scaffold_codex_hooks` writes REAL COPIES (codex_hooks.rs:90), and the module header at :10 says "ONE SET OF SCRIPTS, TWO WIRINGS. The handlers are NOT forked per vendor." Ten symlinks cost git one body; ten copies cost a second body of already-tracked content. OUR SET COMPARISON WAS RIGHT ABOUT NAMES AND SILENT ABOUT STORAGE FORM — and storage form decides it.

I tested the new rule in a scratch repo carrying ONLY this PR's `.gitignore`, so no `.git/info/exclude` line could stand in for it: `.codex/hooks/*.sh` IGNORED, `hooks.json` IGNORED, `config.toml` and `skills/` trackable, root dotfiles ignored. Every `.codex/` member is now decided and nothing is left untracked-and-unignored.

#2066 SPIKE-85 APPROVED at bb84dc4c8d. Both findings discharged, the refuted one correctly left alone ("TUI seam" still occurs once, in its original row), and it exceeded the brief twice:

  - The pre-commit provenance row NARROWS BUG-1578 rather than padding the table. It argues that gate is NOT an instance, because a docs-only diff contains no staged `*.rs` lines so its governed category is empty by construction. I verified the pathspec: aida-pre-commit.sh:300 is `--diff-filter=ACDMR -- '*.rs'`. A rework that narrows a bug its own spec filed is the opposite of the failure I was watching for.
  - THE SELF-DEMONSTRATION IS NOW EVIDENCE, NOT INFERENCE. It cites run 35664201628 on ac772eaca9, and I checked it at STEP level rather than trusting the citation:

        CI docs-only short-circuit                         success
        External-prose classifier inventory                skipped
        Run MCP doc-consistency test                       skipped
        Doc-intent gate                                    skipped
        CLI-manual drift-guard                             skipped

    The four doc gates did not run on the artifact reporting that they do not run — observed, with a run id. Your instruction that the lane verify the ci.yml line numbers itself rather than copy mine is why this is citable.

#2065 BUG-1471 APPROVED at 779cd25f03, AND HERE IS MY CORRECTION.

F1 WAS REAL AND IS FIXED AT THE SEAM, better than I asked. I wanted a third bucket; the lane made `render_spec_card` iterate `card_rel_sections(rels)` so EVERY heading renders from one place, with the invariant written down — "an edge that lands in no bucket is worse than one under a rough heading". `Custom(_) => "Custom"` is kept, not reverted, and `card_rel_edge_name` prints the edge's real name inline.

F2 AND F3 WERE FALSE FINDINGS. There WAS an implementer decision comment, at 22:27:24Z, two minutes before the 22:29 commit, and it carries both things I said were missing: the option-(a) decision with (b) and (c) rejected and reasoned, AND "Store audit… found 139 exact !Custom related edges across 86 spec YAML objects. They are deliberately left as-is (not silently migrated)" with the reason. A count, a disposition, a rationale — criteria 2 and 3 were satisfied at the head I refused.

THE MECHANISM, because it is the useful part: in that YAML a comment's `content:` PRECEDES its `created_at:`. I anchored a read on the timestamp and scanned FORWARD, printing the NEXT record's metadata instead of this record's body, and concluded from that empty window that no such comment existed. Reading a bounded window from the wrong end — the same family as reporting a length from a truncated list, which is the fourth time today the failure has been a bounded read rather than a wrong judgement.

That cost the lane a round on two criteria that were already met. The rework improved discoverability anyway — the reasoning now sits in the PR body and TASK-1426 exists for the migration — and the lane's own framing is fairer than mine deserved: recorded in a comment the diff does not point at is a weaker failure than silence, but still a failure.

ONE FACT FROM THAT ROUND WORTH KEEPING: the inert population grew 128 -> 158 while the fix sat unmerged. The growth argument cuts OPPOSITE to how it reads — the faster it grows, the more the bounded fix wants to land alone rather than behind an 86-object rewrite of the shared store. And the hard reason to defer is independent of timing: 14 twins become 14 duplicates under blind conversion, and the `rel remove --type related` mechanism that may be manufacturing them is unverified.

ALL THREE HOLDS ARE MINE AND I CANNOT CLEAR ANY OF THEM — `merge-hold clear` refuses a non-TTY seat. #2065, #2066 and #2067 each need `aida merge-hold clear <n>` from a terminal. I am not routing around that via `pr ship`.

#2069 (BUG-1520) and #2070 (cli-surface 185/186) are up with no verdict; I have not started them. #2068 remains APPROVED at b0e382d282.
subject: Three reworks APPROVED (#2065 #2066 #2067) — and two of my three findings on #2065 were FALSE; there was a decision comment 2 min before the commit
